blocks.text: This article describes how to determine whether a URL wasn't inspected due to an undecryptable traffic block.
The Zscaler service considers a transaction undecryptable in the following scenarios:

blocks.item: Unsupported cipher suites: The website being accessed uses one of the following ciphers that Zscaler does not support: EXP, DSS, RC4-MD5, RC4-SHA, DES-CBC-SHA, DES-CBC3-SHA, 3DES-CBC-SHA. To learn more, see Supported Cipher Suites in SSL Inspection. An example of traffic destined to a website with unsupported ciphers shows Blocked due to Server Probe failure in the Policy Action column and the SSL Policy reason shows Not Inspected because of undecryptable traffic.

Application traffic that generates non-web traffic over SSL: The Zscaler service allows you to configure HTTPS Services under Services Forwarded to HTTP Web Proxy. If any applications send non-SSL traffic using the ports configured for HTTPS Services, the Zscaler service identifies such transactions as undecryptable traffic.

blocks.text: Verify that the server does not use any unsupported cipher suites.

blocks.heading: Use an External Tool to Validate the Server's SSL Configuration

blocks.text: To learn more, see How to Validate the SSL Configuration of a Web Server.

blocks.item: If you trust a specific domain that requires non-SSL communication using HTTPS ports, you can either configure a rule for that domain with Do Not Inspect action or disable the Block Undecryptable Traffic option.

If an application's traffic to a nonstandard TCP port is considered undecryptable, review whether your organization accesses any HTTPS applications over that port and accordingly update the services configured as HTTPS Services under Administration > Advanced Settings > Services Forwarded to HTTP Web Proxy. To learn more, see Configuring Advanced Settings.
If none of the above steps help, please submit a case to Zscaler Support with the following information:

If you enabled Remote Assistance, the URL and the timestamp when a user tried accessing the web application via the Zscaler service. Otherwise, send the Web Insights logs showing all the columns for the relevant transactions.
Client packet capture (if Zscaler Client Connector is installed).
